payload.summary: Refined roadmap item ri-04 (roadmap-supervisor-orchestration) into a plan that routes every supervise gate through skills/shared/approval_gate.py: a ninth roadmap_approval gate in the trust-posture contract, a single gate_router.py seam in the supervise skill, and an approval_ref that must resolve to a recorded gate decision. Coordinated tier (coordinator reachable). Gate 1 and Gate 2 were satisfied by the roadmap's standing approval (ri-04 approved in roadmap.yaml; operator instruction 'start with ri-04'), per the supervise inherited-approval contract; no per-item questions were asked.

decisions.title: Add a ninth gate, roadmap_approval, instead of reusing proposal_approval
decisions.rationale: Roadmap approval authorizes a DAG of items; proposal approval authorizes one change. Operators must set them independently. Absent/omitted entry resolves to block, preserving fail-closed behaviour.

decisions.title: gate_router.py is the only supervise path to ApprovalGate
decisions.rationale: One seam makes 'no gate decision bypasses approval_gate.py' testable by AST scan and gives every decision a decision_id, source, and correlation ids in the checkpoint gate_decisions sidecar.

decisions.title: approval_ref = gate-decision:<decision_id> and must resolve
decisions.rationale: ExecutionAdapter.resume and prepare verify the reference against the checkpoint ledger (outcome proceed, matching gate and dispatch). The opaque-string path is removed; the only callers were tests.

decisions.title: Parked children check the filed coordinator approval before re-filing
decisions.rationale: Avoids one approval request per supervise cycle under notify_with_timeout while still honouring hot-reloaded posture flips.

decisions.title: Change branch is based on the roadmap branch, not main
decisions.rationale: openspec/roadmap-roadmap-supervisor-orchestration contains main plus 108 commits including the ri-03 supervise seam; main lacks them.

next_steps: Implement wp-contracts first (tasks 1.1-1.5): tests for the ninth gate, then enum/template/schemas, then the shared console_decision helper.
Then wp-router and wp-skill-docs in parallel; wp-integration resyncs mirrors and runs each skills suite in its own process as CI does.
